items.defect: Rationale B overstates the passage claim: 'No sea route through the Americas had been found in 1507, and none would be found in this period.' Magellan found the Strait of Magellan in 1520, a sea route from the Atlantic to the Pacific around the southern tip of South America, within Period 1 (1491-1607). The intended point is the Northwest Passage through North America, which was never found. Fix: 'No Northwest Passage through North America had been found in 1507, and none was ever found.' Key D is sound and the blind pick matched.

Rationales A and D both repeat the error the Lesson 2 fix round already corrected in the lesson: 'Columbus sailed in October of the same year.' Columbus sailed August 3, 1492 and LANDED October 12, 1492. The stem itself correctly says 'In October 1492 Columbus landed in the Caribbean,' and general step 2 correctly says 'Columbus landed in the Caribbean,' so the two rationales contradict the item's own stem. Fix rationale D to 'Granada fell in January and Columbus landed in the Caribbean in October of the same year.' and rationale A to 'Spain took Granada by war in January 1492 and Columbus landed in October of the same year.' Key D is sound and the blind pick matched.

Rubric criteria 2 and 3 carry swapped skill labels: criterion 2 (broader historical context) is labeled 6.B and criterion 3 (supports its argument with at least two specific pieces of evidence) is labeled 4.B. Per cb-codes.json, 4.B is Contextualization and 6.B is support-an-argument-with-evidence, and the settled pattern in LEQs 0005-0011 is thesis 6.A, context 4.B, evidence 6.B, analysis 6.B. This is the same defect fixed in LEQs 0005-0008 in the Topic 1.5 fix round; LEQ 0004 was missed. Fix: criterion 2 skill 6.B to 4.B, criterion 3 skill 4.B to 6.B. The prompt, model outline, and rubric wording are sound; the blind outline scored 6/6 against the rubric.

defects: 'Ten years later, Vasco da Gama sailed on to India, the first European to reach Asia by sea.' Overstates the claim: 5 Steps supports da Gama as the first to open a direct link between Europe and India. Europeans had reached Asia by sea before in other senses (the Mediterranean/Levant), and the standard claim is India, not Asia. Fix: 'the first European to reach India by sea.'

'Johannes Stradanus drew the engraving below around 1600.' Stradanus designed the image; the Galle workshop engraved it. The lesson's own Figure 3 caption correctly says 'Engraving after Johannes Stradanus.' Fix: 'Johannes Stradanus designed the engraving below around 1600.'

method: Lesson read end to end as a student first (doubts recorded before checking books); all 28 questions blind-solved from the blind files only, solves recorded before opening any question file; then adjudicated against keys/model answers/rubrics, checked against Barron's Premium 2027 Ch. 3, 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Ch. 6, and Princeton Review Ch. 6 (033_c006_sup.xhtml), and the Stradanus and Las Casas images viewed. Programmatic checks: option length tells none; key distribution A6/B6/C5/D5; general rationales 78-99 words; SAQ model answers 2 sentences per part; lesson sections 289-300 words, narrative 1,527 words; no paragraph over 90 words; no trap language; frontmatter tie-out 28/28; worked items 9/9 verbatim; all 8 key terms used by bank questions.
notes: Student-read note, not a defect: John Cabot (1497) appears only in MCQ 0052's stem, not in the lesson. Fair, because the stem supplies the fact and the item tests the explore-early/settle-late pattern, not prior knowledge of Cabot.
Student-read note, not a defect: SAQ 0013 part (c) legitimately requires knowledge beyond the stimulus (religious turmoil, war with Spain); the lesson teaches it.

Barron's Ch. 3 repeats its known error 'St. Augustine, Florida (1585)'; the lesson correctly uses 1565 and does not copy it. Barron's 'Columbus made two more voyages' (three total) is also not copied; the lesson correctly says four voyages.

Facts absent from the three books' chapters as extracted (Constantinople 1453, Granada/Reconquista, Sagres, Waldseemuller 1507, Vespucci, Cabral 1500, Verrazano 1524, Fort Caroline, Menendez, Tordesillas 370 leagues, Cape Verde, de Bry 1594) were checked against standard history and are all correct as written.
